claims: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) notes that several small asteroids, including 2026 FM3 (car-sized), are making close flybys of Earth in late March 2026, posing no risk.
NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and Space state that 2026 FM3 is a ~15-foot car-sized asteroid.
NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) and Space state that 2026 FM3 passed within 148,000 miles of Earth on March 24–25, 2026.
148,000 miles is roughly 62% of the distance to the Moon.
NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) states that 2026 FG4 is a ~22-foot bus-sized asteroid passing on March 25, 2026.
NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) states that 2026 EP3 is a ~73-foot airplane-sized asteroid passing on March 25, 2026.
NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) states that 2026 FB3 is a ~55-foot house-sized asteroid passing on March 26, 2026.
Newsweek notes that NASA continues to track the asteroids 2026 FM3, 2026 FG4, 2026 EP3, and 2026 FB3 to refine their orbits and ensure long-term safety.
